problem.name_latex: Symmetric decision problems and graph property testing
problem.name: Symmetric decision problems and graph property testing
problem.statement_latex:
Let $P\subseteq\Sigma^N$ and $f:P\to\{0,1\}$ be invariant under every permutation of the $N$ input positions. Given oracle access to $x\in P$, determine $f(x)$. For graph properties, require invariance under vertex relabeling and specify either adjacency-matrix or adjacency-list access. In the latter model, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the graph family of maximum degree five defined by Ben-David et al., Section 6, with tree-depth parameter $k\ge 1$. Given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and a neighbor oracle $[N]\times[5]\to[N]\cup\{\bot\}$ for an undirected multigraph $G=(V,E)$, $|V|=N$, distinguish
\[
G\in\mathcal P_k
\quad\text{from}\quad
|E\mathbin{\triangle}E'|\ge\varepsilon N
\ \text{for every }G'=(V,E')\in\mathcal P_k,
\]
with error at most $1/3$. Edge edits count multiplicity; self-loops and parallel edges are allowed. These models describe the role of symmetry and input access in quantum speedups. Complexity is measured in the corresponding input-symbol, adjacency-matrix, or neighbor-oracle queries.

quantum.headline_latex: $(k/\varepsilon)^{O(1)}$ queries for $\mathcal P_k$, quantum-walk property testing; $Q(f)$ for the symmetric decision problems.
quantum.details_latex: The tester identifies weld vertices by quantum walks and checks the graph structure locally. It has perfect completeness and rejects $\varepsilon$-far inputs with probability at least $2/3$. Here $Q(f)$ and $R(f)$ denote bounded-error quantum and randomized query complexity; each comparison uses the same promise and oracle representation.

classical.headline_latex: $\exp(\Omega(k))$ queries required for $\mathcal P_k$ at a fixed constant $\varepsilon>0$, and $O(N)$ sufficient by reading the graph; $O(Q(f)^3)$ for full permutation symmetry, Chailloux's simulation.
classical.details_latex: The lower bound holds for every bounded-error randomized tester. Reading the adjacency lists permits exact membership testing with unrestricted offline computation. For adjacency-matrix graph properties, $R(f)=O(Q(f)^6)$; for fixed $r$-uniform hypergraphs, $R(f)=O(Q(f)^{3r})$.

strength.description_latex: Exponential to polynomial query complexity in $k$ for adjacency-list testing of $\mathcal P_k$. Full permutation symmetry and adjacency-matrix graph symmetry impose the stated polynomial limits.

evidence.description_latex: Unconditional classical query lower bounds establish the adjacency-list separation; classical simulation theorems establish the limits in the other models.
